_about: Hand-written facts for notable team-seasons, keyed SEASON-TEAM (team code as used that season). Used instead of generated facts when that team-season is the subject of a round.
1999-STL: Led by Kurt Warner, a former grocery-store stocker who began the year as a backup, the 'Greatest Show on Turf' Rams won Super Bowl XXXIV.
1999-TEN: The Titans survived the playoffs on the 'Music City Miracle' kickoff return, then lost Super Bowl XXXIV when Kevin Dyson was stopped a yard short on the final play.
2000-BAL: The Ravens allowed just 165 points, a record for a 16-game season, and won Super Bowl XXXV.
2001-NE: Tom Brady took over after Drew Bledsoe was injured in Week 2, and the Patriots upset the Rams to win Super Bowl XXXVI.
2002-TB: The Buccaneers had the NFL's best defense and won Super Bowl XXXVII over the Raiders, the team their coach Jon Gruden had led the year before.
2002-HOU: In their first-ever game, the expansion Texans beat the Cowboys 19-10.
2003-NE: The Patriots won their last 12 regular-season games and beat the Panthers in Super Bowl XXXVIII.
2003-CAR: The Panthers reached their first Super Bowl and lost 32-29 to the Patriots on a field goal in the final seconds.
2004-NE: The Patriots won back-to-back titles, beating the Eagles in Super Bowl XXXIX.
2004-IND: Peyton Manning threw 49 touchdown passes, breaking Dan Marino's single-season record of 48.
2005-PIT: The Steelers won Super Bowl XL as the AFC's 6th seed, winning three straight playoff games on the road first.
2005-SEA: Shaun Alexander won MVP with 27 rushing touchdowns, and the Seahawks reached their first Super Bowl.
2006-SD: LaDainian Tomlinson scored an NFL-record 31 touchdowns and won MVP.
2006-IND: Peyton Manning won his first Super Bowl, beating the Bears in a rain-soaked Super Bowl XLI.
2007-NE: The Patriots went 16-0 and scored a then-record 589 points as Tom Brady threw 50 TDs and Randy Moss caught 23, but lost Super Bowl XLII to the Giants.
2007-NYG: The 10-6 Giants ended the Patriots' perfect season in Super Bowl XLII, helped by David Tyree's helmet catch.
2007-MIA: The Dolphins went 1-15; their only win came in overtime against the Ravens in Week 15.
2008-DET: The Lions became the first team to finish a season 0-16.
2008-MIA: A year after going 1-15, the Dolphins went 11-5 and won the AFC East, popularizing the 'Wildcat' formation.
2008-ARI: Kurt Warner led the Cardinals to their first Super Bowl, which they lost to the Steelers on a late Santonio Holmes touchdown.
2008-PIT: The Steelers won Super Bowl XLIII, their record-setting sixth Super Bowl title.
2009-NO: The Saints started 13-0 and won their first Super Bowl, beating the Colts in Super Bowl XLIV.
2009-IND: The Colts started 14-0 before resting their starters, then lost Super Bowl XLIV to the Saints.
2010-SEA: The Seahawks became the first team to win a division with a losing record, then upset the Saints in the playoffs behind Marshawn Lynch's 'Beast Quake' run.
2010-GB: The Packers won Super Bowl XLV as the NFC's 6th seed.
2011-GB: The Packers went 15-1 and Aaron Rodgers won MVP, but they lost their first playoff game to the Giants.
2011-NYG: The Giants went just 9-7 in the regular season, then beat the Patriots in Super Bowl XLVI.
2011-IND: With Peyton Manning out for the year after neck surgery, the Colts fell to 2-14 and drafted Andrew Luck first overall.
2012-IND: Rookie Andrew Luck led the Colts to the playoffs one year after they went 2-14.
2012-MIN: Adrian Peterson ran for 2,097 yards, nine short of Eric Dickerson's single-season record, and won MVP.
2012-BAL: In Ray Lewis's final season, the Ravens beat the 49ers in Super Bowl XLVII.
2013-DEN: The Broncos scored an NFL-record 606 points as Peyton Manning threw a record 55 touchdown passes.
2013-SEA: The Seahawks had the NFL's stingiest defense and crushed the Broncos 43-8 in Super Bowl XLVIII.
2014-CAR: The Panthers won the NFC South with a losing 7-8-1 record.
2014-NE: The Patriots beat the Seahawks in Super Bowl XLIX, sealed by Malcolm Butler's goal-line interception.
2015-CAR: The Panthers went 15-1 and Cam Newton won MVP, but they lost Super Bowl 50 to the Broncos.
2015-DEN: In Peyton Manning's final season, the Broncos' top-ranked defense carried them to a Super Bowl 50 win.
2016-NE: The Patriots came back from 28-3 down to beat the Falcons in overtime in Super Bowl LI.
2016-ATL: The Falcons led the NFL in scoring and led Super Bowl LI 28-3 before losing to the Patriots in overtime.
2016-CLE: The Browns went 1-15; their only win came on Christmas Eve against the Chargers.
2017-CLE: The Browns went 0-16, joining the 2008 Lions as the only teams to lose every game of a 16-game season.
2017-PHI: Backup QB Nick Foles replaced an injured Carson Wentz and led the Eagles to their first Super Bowl title.
2017-MIN: The Vikings beat the Saints in the playoffs on the 'Minneapolis Miracle', a 61-yard touchdown on the final play.
2018-KC: In his first full season as a starter, Patrick Mahomes threw 50 touchdown passes and won MVP.
2018-NE: The Patriots beat the Rams 13-3 in Super Bowl LIII, the lowest-scoring Super Bowl ever.
2018-LA: The Rams reached the Super Bowl but managed just 3 points in a loss to the Patriots.
2019-BAL: Lamar Jackson was the unanimous MVP, and the Ravens set an NFL record for team rushing yards.
2019-KC: The Chiefs won their first Super Bowl in 50 years, rallying from 10 points down in the fourth quarter against the 49ers.
2019-SF: A year after going 4-12, the 49ers went 13-3 and reached Super Bowl LIV, losing to the Chiefs.
2020-TB: In Tom Brady's first season in Tampa, the Buccaneers became the first team to win a Super Bowl in their home stadium.
2020-CLE: The Browns made the playoffs for the first time since 2002 and won a playoff game in Pittsburgh.
2021-LA: The Rams won Super Bowl LVI in their home stadium, one year after the Buccaneers did the same.
2021-CIN: The Bengals reached their first Super Bowl in 33 years, losing to the Rams.
2022-PHI: The Eagles went 14-3 but lost Super Bowl LVII 38-35 to the Chiefs.
2022-KC: Patrick Mahomes won his second MVP, and the Chiefs beat the Eagles 38-35 in Super Bowl LVII.
2023-KC: The Chiefs won back-to-back titles, beating the 49ers in overtime in Super Bowl LVIII.
2023-DET: The Lions won their first division title in 30 years.
2024-PHI: Saquon Barkley ran for 2,005 yards, and the Eagles beat the Chiefs 40-22 in Super Bowl LIX.
2024-DET: The Lions went 15-2, the best record in franchise history.
2024-MIN: The Vikings went 14-3 and still had to play on the road as a wild card, because Detroit won the division.
